verses.1: For the choirmaster. On lilies. A psalm of David.
verses.2: Rescue me, God, for the waters have reached my life.
verses.3: I have sunk into mire and have no foothold. I have come into deep waters, and the storm has swept over me.
verses.4: I have cried out in distress, my throat has failed, my eyes have grown weary from waiting for my God.
verses.5: Many more than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause. My adversaries are strong—those who attack me unjustly. I did not steal, and yet they accuse me.
verses.6: God, you know my foolishness, and my sins are not hidden from you.
verses.7: Let your servants not be put to shame, LORD of Hosts, nor those who seek you be humiliated, O God of Israel.
verses.8: Because of you I have borne disgrace, and shame has covered my face.
verses.9: I have become a stranger to my brothers, a foreigner to the children of my mother.
verses.10: For the zeal for your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
verses.11: I have fasted and my soul grows faint, and it has become a reproach to me.
verses.12: I have clothed myself with sackcloth, and I have become a proverb to them.
verses.13: Those who sit at the gate gossip about me, and those who drink wine sing songs about me.
verses.14: But you, O LORD, in the time of your favor, by the abundance of your steadfast love, answer me in truth, your salvation.
verses.15: Rescue me from the mire, or I will sink. Set me free from my enemies and from the depths of the waters.
verses.16: Do not let the storm sweep me away, nor let the abyss swallow me, nor let the pit close its mouth over me.
verses.17: Hear me, LORD, for your steadfast love is good. Look toward me in your great mercy.
verses.18: Turn not your face from your servant, for I am in distress; answer me quickly.
verses.19: Draw near to my soul and redeem it, deliver me because of my enemies.
verses.20: You, O God, know my disgrace and my shame and my dishonor. All those who oppress me are before you.
verses.21: My heart has expected reproach and pain, and I have waited for comfort, but there was none. I have waited for someone to console me, but I found none.
verses.22: They gave me gall for food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
verses.23: Let their table before them become a trap, and a snare for those at peace.
verses.24: Let their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and let their loins always be seized with trembling.
verses.25: Pour out your anger on them, and let the heat of your wrath overtake them.
verses.26: Let their dwellings be desolate, with no one to live in them.
verses.27: For you are the one who struck, and they pursued. Let their wounds be added to their pain.
verses.28: Add guilt to their guilt, and let them not enter your righteousness.
verses.29: Let them be blotted out from the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.
verses.30: But I, though poor and in pain, have had your salvation. O God, you have strengthened me.
verses.31: I will praise the name of God with a song, and I will magnify him with thanksgiving.
verses.32: And it will please the LORD more than young bulls, with horns and hooves.
verses.33: The poor will see it and rejoice, those who seek God will live, and your hearts will revive.
verses.34: For the LORD hears the poor, and he does not despise those in bondage.
verses.35: Let the heavens and the earth praise him, the sea and all that moves within it.
verses.36: For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah, and they will dwell there and possess it.
verses.37: And the seed of his servants will inherit it, and those who love his name will dwell in it.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "On lilies" is a musical term; its exact meaning is uncertain.
- v. 5: "I did not steal, and yet they accuse me" reflects the speaker’s unjust treatment.
- v. 11: "it has become a reproach to me" refers to the fast becoming a subject of mockery.
- v. 12: "I have become a proverb to them" indicates the speaker is the subject of a common saying or joke.
- v. 22: "they gave me gall for food" and "vinegar to drink" are symbolic of cruel treatment.
- v. 23: "a trap" and "a snare" are metaphors for divine judgment on the wicked.
- v. 27: "Let their wounds be added to their pain" is a call for retribution.
- v. 32: "more than young bulls, with horns and hooves" is a poetic reference to sacrificial offerings.
